brown-beast-facing-left.description: A brown dragon-like quadruped walks to the left on four clawed feet, with a long arched neck, an open mouth, a pointed ear and a long tail that curls into a spiral behind it with a gold trefoil inside the curl. The body is brown with small cream drop-shaped marks and black contours, with thin green fringes from the initial's ground along parts of the outline; the background is transparent.

provenance.date: First half of the 14th century CE

brown-beast-facing-left.quality: Thin green fringes from the painted ground of the initial remain along parts of the outline.
brown-beast-facing-left.title: Brown beast with trefoil in its tail, facing left
usage_notes: The gold trefoil inside the tail curl belongs to the piece; in the initial the two beasts face each other, so this one pairs with brown-quadruped-facing-right on the other side of a title or heading.

brown-beast-facing-right.description: A brown dragon-like quadruped walks to the right on four clawed feet, with a long arched neck, an open mouth, a pointed ear and a long tail that curls into a spiral behind it with a gold trefoil inside the curl. The body is brown with small cream drop-shaped marks and black contours, with thin green fringes from the initial's ground along parts of the outline; the background is transparent.

provenance.date: First half of the 14th century CE

brown-beast-facing-right.quality: Thin green fringes from the painted ground of the initial remain along parts of the outline.
brown-beast-facing-right.title: Brown beast with trefoil in its tail, facing right
usage_notes: The gold trefoil inside the tail curl belongs to the piece; in the initial the two beasts face each other, so this one pairs with brown-quadruped-facing-left on the other side of a title or heading.

corner-top-left.description: Top-left mitred corner cut from the same initial, a gray-blue four-lobed leaf in a gold roundel with the red rule turning the inner angle; transparent along its outer top and left edges.

corner-top-right.description: Alternative top-right corner from the same initial with a red four-lobed leaf in its roundel; the atlas does not use it, place it by hand.

lobed-leaves-in-gold-medallions.description: One cycle of a horizontal band: three burnished gold roundels ringed in olive green hold a red, a blue and a gray-blue lobed leaf on a dark ground, joined by green stems with small curled leaves between them; a thin red rule with a pale line runs along the bottom edge. The pattern continues across the left and right edges; the strip above the band and a thinner one below the red rule are transparent.

provenance.date: First half of the 14th century CE

lobed-leaves-in-gold-medallions.quality: The join at the ends is averaged over a two-column collar; the three roundels differ slightly in brushwork, as painted.
lobed-leaves-in-gold-medallions.title: Lobed leaves in gold medallions, repeat tile
usage_notes: Repeat along x; the generated rotated tile gives the vertical band. The red rule is the inner edge, keep it toward the framed content.
The frame atlas mirrors corner-top-left into all four corners, so every corner carries the gray-blue leaf; corner-top-right is the red-leaf variant for hand-built frames.

corner-top-left.description: Top-left corner cut from the same initial, a red three-lobed leaf in a triangular compartment of the ribbon with the red rule turning the inner angle; transparent along its outer top and left edges. Its painted field is 517 px deep against the band's 419 px, so it is for hand-built frames only.

corner-top-right.description: Top-right corner from the same initial with its red leaf arranged for the right-hand angle, same depth as corner-top-left; for hand-built frames only.

opposed-leaves-with-gray-interlace.description: One cycle of a vertical band on burnished gold: a pale gray-mauve ribbon outlined in black loops into four heart-shaped compartments on a dark ground, the outer two holding red three-lobed leaves that point outward and the middle two blue leaves that point in toward each other; a red rule with a white line runs along the left edge. The pattern continues across the top and bottom edges and the band is fully opaque.

provenance.date: First half of the 14th century CE

opposed-leaves-with-gray-interlace.quality: The join at the ends is averaged over a two-column collar; the gold ground keeps the crackle of the leaf.
opposed-leaves-with-gray-interlace.title: Opposed leaves in gray interlace, repeat tile
usage_notes: Repeat along y; the generated rotated tile gives the horizontal band. The red rule is the inner edge, keep it toward the framed content.

No frame atlas: the corners are about 98 px deeper than the band inside the red rule and would protrude into the framed area, so build a frame by hand from the band and the two corner components, aligning the red rules.

three-gold-trefoils-on-serpentine-scroll.description: A burnished gold band winds in a serpentine from a large spiral at the left through two smaller loops to a jagged cut end at the right, each loop holding a gold three-lobed trefoil, with a short tendril dropping from the lower curve. Thin black contours edge the gold, which keeps the crackled texture of the leaf and a faint pale paper line along some edges; the background is transparent.

provenance.date: First half of the 14th century CE

three-gold-trefoils-on-serpentine-scroll.quality: Right end cut at the junction with the letter; a faint pale paper contour follows parts of the gold edge.
three-gold-trefoils-on-serpentine-scroll.title: Gold scroll with three trefoils
usage_notes: The right end is cut where the scroll met the stroke of the letter S; use it as the trailing end of a flourish or tuck it under another element.
